src/routes/cardsRouter.ts: cardsRouter.post("/create", apiKeyValidator, bodySchemaValidator(createCardSchema), create) and similar put routes for /activate, /block, /unblock
src/routes/statementsRouter.ts: statementsRouter.post("/recharge", apiKeyValidator, bodySchemaValidator(rechargeSchema), recharge) follows the same middleware-then-controller pattern

parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/routes module has one cohesive concern: declaring HTTP routes in Express. router.ts only combines the two sub-routers. cardsRouter.ts covers card lifecycle routes (create, create virtual, activate, block, unblock). statementsRouter.ts covers balance and transaction routes (statement, recharge, buy, buy online). Both sub-routers build routes the same way: Router() plus optional apiKeyValidator plus bodySchemaValidator(schema) plus a controller handler. Validation rules live in the external schema modules and are not repeated here; blockCardSchema is reused for /block and /unblock rather than copied. No route bypasses the controller abstraction or puts logic inline. One minor point: statementsRouter.ts imports getStatement from cardsController, so the router and controller grouping differ slightly, but the route still fits the statements concern and no rule is duplicated or bypassed. apiKeyValidator is only on some routes, which looks like deliberate domain design, not a duplicated invariant.
